body:
This looks good to me. I traced the issue as you outlined in the original issue and agree this is the simplest and best fix. I tested and agree this fixes the issue. 

When duplicating nodes with auto-generated names (e.g., `@Node@2`), I would expect that the duplicated nodes' names would also have "@" in them, like the originals, so removing the name sanitization in `Node::_duplicate` makes sense.

There are other differences between `set_name` and `_set_name_no_check` that fortunately will have no difference when changing to `_set_name_no_check`, so this change looks perfectly safe to me. The differences are:
- `set_name` calls `_release_unique_name_in_owner()` and then `_acquire_unique_name_in_owner()` if the node has an owner and `unique_name_in_owner == true` but these will be false at this point when called in `_duplicate`.
- If the node has a parent, `set_name` does `data.parent->_validate_child_name(this, true);`. Since duplication is recursive, all the recursively duplicated children won't have `set_name` call the `_validate_child_name`, but `_duplicate` later calls `add_child` on them anyways at [node.cpp:2934](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/scene/main/node.cpp#L2934) so this isn't an issue (`add_child` calls `_validate_child_name` anyways).
